newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean yields close lower on fewer new issues.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean yields close lower on fewer new issues.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporates closed lower on Wednesday as fewer new issues amid ample liquidity at financial institutions boosted buying sentiment, brokers said.
The sentiment was little affected by the Bank of Korea's absorption of one trillion won through repurchase agreements.
Three-month CD yields and overnight call rate also fell in active trading, they said.
* 3-yr corporates end at 11.98 pct vs 12.13 pct on Tuesday
* 3-mth CDs close at 12.45 pct vs 12.60 pct
* Overnight call average 11.81 pct vs 12.01 pct
The central bank absorbed the surplus liquidity through six-day repurchase agreements.
Brokers said liquidity remained high among financial institutions as they were reluctant to give loans in fears of corportate failures.
"The three-year yields would test 11.90 percent on Thursday. Buying sentiment will remain strong for the time being," said Lee Chang-woo of Samsung Securities.
Three-month CD yields and overnight call rate also closed lower in active trading, they said.
